reading.body:
Miro is a visual collaboration platform with AI features for diagram generation and note synthesis, positioned as a hub where teams integrate outputs from external AI tools like Claude rather than replacing them.

The company's strategy reflects a narrowing of AI's role in creative work. Miro does not claim to generate designs from scratch. Instead it synthesizes research, organizes AI outputs from elsewhere, and converts unstructured team input into structured formats. This is computationally lighter than end-to-end generation, which matters because it reduces the scaling pressure on Miro's own infrastructure. The platform's value sits in orchestration and collective sense-making rather than model size or training data.

The data does not cover Miro's infrastructure footprint, the compute cost of its synthesis features, or whether its AI capabilities are in-house or outsourced. It also does not show user growth, revenue, or competitive positioning against other whiteboard tools. The mention of "creative IP risk" suggests Miro has acknowledged provenance concerns in design workflows, but the extent of that risk or how the product mitigates it remains unclear from the available information.

profile_text.body:
Miro is a for-profit startup founded in 2011 and headquartered in Amsterdam, Netherlands. Its site describes an AI innovation workspace for speeding up product development from ideation to launch, aligning teams, breaking tool silos, and shipping what customers need in one AI-powered visual platform. The site quotes a customer saying that bringing everyone together to plan in Miro means the most impactful initiatives will happen at the right time and customers will get the functionality they want.

The company's tracked product is Miro AI, listed under Image & Graphic Design, described as a collaborative whiteboard AI with diagram generation, sticky note synthesis, and creative IP risk. Two MCP servers are also tracked: ai.waystation/miro, for collaborating on visual boards with a team using the Miro integration, and app.miromiro/miromiro, which turns a live website into brand colors, fonts, design tokens, SVGs, Lottie and paste-ready code.

No lawsuits are recorded for Miro.
